question: How many of the 47 numbered questions in the Commerce Commission's issues paper did none of Vocus, WISPA NZ and Speedchecker set out to answer, and which is the lowest-numbered of them?
step_by_step_reasoning:
Step 1. Source input (Doc 9, Vocus): Vocus heads each part of its response with the questions it is answering. Across the whole response these are Q1, Q2, Q3, Q4, Q5, Q6, Q7, Q13, Q14, Q17, Q18, Q19, Q21, Q22, Q25, Q26, Q37, Q38, Q39, Q40, Q46 and Q47.

Step 2. Source input (Doc 10, WISPA NZ): WISPA NZ says it has not answered every question and stays silent where a question is out of scope for its members. It sets out Q3, Q4, Q14, Q15, Q16, Q20, Q33, Q34, Q40, Q41, Q44 and Q45.

Step 3. Source input (Doc 11, Speedchecker): Speedchecker confines its comments to the questions it has useful information on. It sets out Q2.1, Q7, Q9, Q10, Q27, Q28, Q29, Q30 and Q41.

Step 4. Combining the lists (Doc 9, Doc 10 and Doc 11): some questions are on two lists and count once. Q3, Q4, Q14 and Q40 are on both Vocus's and WISPA NZ's, Q2 and Q7 on both Vocus's and Speedchecker's, and Q41 on both WISPA NZ's and Speedchecker's. Together the three set out to answer Q1 to Q7, Q9, Q10, Q13 to Q22, Q25 to Q30, Q33, Q34, Q37 to Q41 and Q44 to Q47.

Step 5. Result (Doc 9, Doc 10 and Doc 11): the questions left over, which none of the three set out to answer, are Q8, Q11, Q12, Q23, Q24, Q31, Q32, Q35, Q36, Q42 and Q43. That is 11 questions, and the lowest-numbered is Q8.

why_these_are_traps: Linking across documents: seven questions appear in two respondents' lists (Q3, Q4, Q14, Q40 in Doc 9 and Doc 10; Q2, Q7 in Doc 9 and Doc 11; Q41 in Doc 10 and Doc 11). Adding 22, 12 and 9 gives 4. Counted once, 11 remain.
